propositions: The inbound link differ is ADD-only by construction and never emits removal records when a link is deleted in Jira, while the outbound direction has a removal path, creating asymmetric bidirectional sync.

A link deleted in Jira remains on the local ticket indefinitely because no reconciliation pass detects or reports the absence, violating the J11 mutation table row-11 oracle that the link should be absent.
The apply layer silently discards non-add link records via an action-check gate, so even a correct differ emit would never reach the store, making any removal fix inert at the apply boundary.

Inferring peer deletion from local-dep presence plus peer-link absence is unsafe without observing that the peer's link data was positively fetched, risking data loss on failed enrichment or truncated responses.

The ecosystem research and first-hand incident (63 parent edges destroyed by identical inference) show that mirroring peer-side link deletions is deferred in favor of local-wins-and-restore semantics, identical to comparable tools.
